four_way_judging.judge: codex/gpt-5.6-sol, blind, rubric as complete instruction set, file-based rooms, answers de-identified as answer_1..4
findings: Diagnostic prompt (p01): E > D > F > G in BOTH permutations — G last twice despite fluency; its glossary-shaped bundle gives it the least situation-specific material.
Essay prompt (e01): rank-unstable across permutations (G first then last; E last then first) — margins of 1-4 points are noise at this n.
The judges scored G's calibration 9-10 while its underlying bundle carries contradicted formulas: preference rubrics cannot detect fabrication. Finding 4 at arm level.
House-conduct artifacts penalised again: E's markers called 'opaque citation shorthand' (e01 perm1), D's trace called 'extraneous' (e01 perm2).

g_answer_citation_fidelity.notes: All four FILE-NOT-FOUND are shorthand re-citations (bare filenames without paths, no source-key list) — a citation-legibility defect unique to G among the arms; D/E/F had zero unresolvable citations.

laundering_chain: CONFIRMED by content inspection: the balanced-scorecard note invented a requirement ('define a data source, reporting period, and responsible owner') graded UNSUPPORTED-CONTENT against the source; the p01-G answer repeats that invented requirement citing the note; the bundle-level citation audit grades the answer's use of the note as supported. Fabricated content in the intermediate layer propagates into answers and becomes invisible to bundle-level auditing one hop downstream. Only source-level tracing catches it — which is what a corpus-level audit-of-record (Pass I) exists to be.
